key_insight: The Kármán–Howarth equation yields bounded 1/4-power laws for streamwise velocity variance and dissipation in turbulent channel flow.
engineering_relevance: These scaling laws can inform high-Reynolds-number wall-turbulence models by constraining how fluctuation peaks and dissipation approach finite limits.
method: Apply the Kármán–Howarth equation to turbulent channel flow.
Use a logarithmic mean velocity profile and near-isotropy of spatial velocity derivatives.
Derive overlap-region variance scaling as c₁ − c₂(y/δ)^(1/4) and inner-peak scaling as c₁′ − c₂′Re_τ^(−1/4).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations linked to prior scaling results, but provides no quantitative dataset comparisons or validation metrics.
watch_item: Application depends on the validity of the logarithmic-profile and derivative near-isotropy assumptions; extrapolation beyond channel flow requires validation.
paper_title: The 1/4-power law for bounded variation of wall turbulence from the Kármán-Howarth equation
